quantContext.note: From this project's own scoring pipeline (companies.json + screener.js, Phases 1-5/7), included for reference only - not itself a research source.

whyCheapBearCase.answer: MOS trades at a very low P/B (0.65) with a weak ROE (4.72%) [source: 1] - and the filings show this is at least partly justified by a genuine, recent deterioration, not just market pessimism. Mosaic swung from net income of $410.7 million in Q2 2025 to a net LOSS of $272.8 million in Q2 2026, and from operating income of $244.4 million (Q2 2025) to an operating LOSS of $35.5 million (Q2 2026); for the first half of the year, net income of roughly $648.8 million in H1 2025 (derived by subtracting the disclosed Q3 2025 figure of $411.4 million from the disclosed nine-month cumulative figure of $1,060.2 million) became a net LOSS of $530.4 million in H1 2026 [source: 2]. The 10-Q's Risk Factors updates explicitly flag that key raw material costs (sulfur, ammonia, natural gas) have been volatile and that disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz - tied to heightened tensions involving Iran - have adversely affected the availability, cost, and timing of sulfur and ammonia inputs, with no assurance the company can pass these costs through given its products are largely commodities [source: 3]. A cached Q2 2026 earnings-call headline, 'Navigating Sulfur-Driven Curtailments,' is consistent with this being the proximate driver of the swing to losses [source: 6]. Mosaic also faces an active antitrust multidistrict litigation (putative class actions alleging anticompetitive fertilizer pricing conduct, consolidated for pretrial in the District of Kansas in June 2026) [source: 4], an added overhang. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: the pipeline's extraction of the 10-Q's actual MD&A results-discussion text failed - it captured only boilerplate 'Item 4 Controls and Procedures' language rather than management's narrative explanation of the quarter - so I could not directly quote management's own explanation of the Q2 2026 loss; the account above is built from XBRL figures, the Risk Factors update, and a single earnings-call headline rather than a full MD&A narrative.

revenueEpsTrend.answer: Deteriorating in the most recent quarters, following a genuinely improving FY2025. Per the 10-K, FY2025 net sales were $12,052.4 million vs. $11,122.8 million in FY2024 (+8%), and net earnings attributable to Mosaic were $540.7 million ($1.70 diluted EPS) vs. $174.9 million ($0.55) in FY2024 - a real, filing-confirmed improvement year [source: 5]. That trend reversed sharply in 2026: per XBRL, Q2 2026 revenue was $2,824.1 million vs. $3,005.7 million in Q2 2025 (-6.0%), while H1 2026 revenue of $5,822.1 million was still up 3.5% over H1 2025's $5,626.6 million. Diluted EPS, however, went from +$1.29 in Q2 2025 to -$0.86 in Q2 2026, and -$1.67 for H1 2026 [source: 2]. So revenue held up better than earnings - the swing to losses (detailed in the prior answer) is concentrated in costs/margin, not a topline collapse.

marginTrend.answer: Improving in FY2025, then sharply deteriorating in 2026. The 10-K's Results of Operations table shows FY2025 gross margin of 15.8% vs. 13.6% in FY2024 (+2.2 points), and operating earnings of $821.5 million vs. $621.5 million (+32%) [source: 5]. By contrast, H1 2026 operating income swung to a loss of $408.4 million (from operating income of roughly $582.9 million in H1 2025, derived the same way as the net-income figure above: nine-month cumulative operating income of $922.7 million less the disclosed Q3 2025 figure of $339.8 million) [source: 2] - implying a swing of roughly $1 billion in operating profitability year-over-year. As noted above, the extraction pipeline did not capture a usable MD&A narrative explaining this swing in the 10-Q itself, so this conclusion rests on XBRL figures plus the Risk Factors' input-cost-volatility disclosure and a cached earnings-call headline referencing sulfur-driven curtailments, not a directly quoted management explanation.

guidanceChange.answer: Not determinable from available sources. Neither the extracted 10-Q Risk Factors updates nor the 10-K MD&A/Results-of-Operations text contains an explicit forward-looking numeric guidance range for FY2026. A cached headline references a full Q2 2026 earnings call transcript ('The Mosaic Company (MOS) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript,' SeekingAlpha) that would likely contain guidance commentary, but only the headline was cached, not the article content, so I am not inferring a guidance direction from it [source: 8].

catalysts.text: Active debt tender: on 2026-08-10, Mosaic commenced offers to purchase for cash certain of its outstanding debt securities, a potential deleveraging/balance-sheet management move (debt/equity is already low at 0.066 per the quant data).

Portfolio streamlining continues: the Carlsbad, New Mexico potash mine sale closed April 30, 2026 (cash proceeds of roughly $2 million plus a $10 million deferred payment, following a ~$191.2 million impairment recognized on the disposal group), on top of the 2025 sales of the Patos de Minas phosphate mine and the Taquari potash mine.

FY2025 showed genuine underlying strength before the 2026 cost shock: Potash segment gross margin rose to 32.7% (from 26.9% in FY2024) on higher international demand and selling prices, and total FY2025 net earnings grew 209% YoY - if fertilizer pricing and sulfur/ammonia costs normalize, the earnings base that existed as recently as FY2025 could reassert itself.

risks.text: Sharp, filing-confirmed reversal to net and operating losses in H1 2026 versus a profitable FY2025 - real and current, not resolved as of the 10-Q filing date.

Active antitrust multidistrict litigation: putative class actions alleging anticompetitive conduct in fertilizer pricing, consolidated for coordinated pretrial proceedings in the District of Kansas as of June 9, 2026.

Explicitly disclosed commodity input-cost volatility: sulfur, ammonia, and natural gas costs tied to geopolitical disruptions (Strait of Hormuz tensions involving Iran, the Russia-Ukraine conflict), with no assurance these costs can be passed through given Mosaic's products are largely commodities.
Ongoing countervailing/antidumping duty litigation related to Moroccan and Russian phosphate imports remains unresolved, with continuing federal court and CIT/CAFC proceedings.

verdict.reasoning: The quant screen's statistical cheapness (P/B 0.65) is real, but the filing evidence shows the weak trailing ROE (4.72%) understates how sharply results have actually deteriorated: Mosaic swung from meaningful profitability in FY2025 (net earnings +209% YoY, $540.7 million) to net losses in both Q1 and Q2 2026, driven at least in part by a sulfur/ammonia cost spike tied to Middle East shipping disruptions that the company itself flags as an ongoing risk factor, plus an unresolved antitrust MDL. This looks more like a company genuinely working through a cost shock than a simple market overreaction to a healthy business - but I can't confirm that read with high confidence because the pipeline failed to extract the 10-Q's actual MD&A narrative (it captured only Item 4 boilerplate), so I have no direct management explanation of whether the H1 2026 loss is transitory (input-cost driven, as the risk factors and one earnings-call headline suggest) or reflects something more structural. Given that gap, I'm flagging this as elevated value-trap risk with low confidence rather than asserting either a clean opportunity or a clean trap.
